# Competitive Moat Review

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. A moat review tests a claim, it does not certify one: a business with no surviving power can still be bought, but not at a price that assumes durability, private equity carries a real risk of loss, and no review here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the competitive moat review skill of the private equity pack in andreworia/claude-finance-skills. Use it after commercial analysis has mapped the landscape and before the exit multiple is set: commercial analysis asks how attractive the industry is, this skill asks whether this company holds anything durable inside it, and it is aimed squarely at every CIM that says highly defensible. The method applies a benefit-and-barrier test first: a power needs a quantified benefit (price, cost or retention a competitor cannot match) and a barrier that stops a well-funded competitor arbitraging it away, with the counterfactual set up front, because a funded entrant reaching parity in under 18 months means there is no moat. Each candidate power from Helmer Seven Powers is then tested on its own evidence in turn: scale economies (does unit cost actually fall with volume, margin plotted against volume over three years), network effects (value or retention rising with density, with data effects noted as flattening early), switching costs (measured in implementation days, integrations, migration, retraining and exit fees, cross-checked...
